read_against: generated/maxharness-prompt-cost-and-duplication-2026-09-20.json and the gate in the bundle manifest, both written before the run

RESULT.verdict: REJECT. The REJECT line was <= 30. Rule 15(c) bars shipping it, permanently.

EVERY_MECHANISM_FIRED_AND_THAT_IS_THE_PO.note: Counters are host-side and readable, in the artifacts/*_events.jsonl stream under type=experiment. They are NOT in viewer_data.json, whose viewer_steps list is empty; look in the events stream.
EVERY_MECHANISM_FIRED_AND_THAT_IS_THE_PO.wm_step_resolved: 506 calls across 18 of 25 games. The harness found and called a step function THE MODEL WROTE.
EVERY_MECHANISM_FIRED_AND_THAT_IS_THE_PO.wm_batch_refused: 18 across 11 games, so the refusal never wedged the agent
EVERY_MECHANISM_FIRED_AND_THAT_IS_THE_PO.steplog_records: 891 across 25 of 25; steplog_helper_calls 100 across 15 of 25, i.e. the model really called the log helpers
EVERY_MECHANISM_FIRED_AND_THAT_IS_THE_PO.consolidation_calls: 15 across 11 games, writing 57,435 bytes of code into memory['prelude']

ADOPTION_TRIPLED_AND_THE_SCORE_HALVED.adoption: Model-authored world model resolved in 18 of 25 games, against GG8's 6 of 25 and GG6's 5 of 25. This is by far the highest formalism adoption this project has ever measured.

THE_MECHANISM_OF_THE_LOSS_IS_ONE_NUMBER.reading: Environment actions per game fall monotonically as world-model machinery is added, and levels fall with them. Max-harness plays ONE THIRD the environment actions of the sampling arm inside the identical 7,920-second clock. Every turn spent writing, validating, searching and consolidating a world model is a turn not spent playing. The machinery does not fail, it DISPLACES play.
THE_MECHANISM_OF_THE_LOSS_IS_ONE_NUMBER.why_this_is_not_an_integration_failure: It is the opposite. The integration worked: adoption tripled, validation ran 3,840 times at a 94% pass rate, the model called the log helpers 100 times unprompted, and the refusal path fired only 18 times. The thesis was tested properly and it lost.

WHAT_THIS_ESTABLISHES.claim: On an open-weight model inside a fixed wall clock, the certify-then-plan architecture trades environment actions for modelling, and on ARC-AGI-3 that trade is bad.
WHAT_THIS_ESTABLISHES.why_it_generalises: Every published instance of this architecture runs a closed frontier model, and several report near-ceiling scores. None reports its environment-actions-per-game against a no-harness control inside a fixed deadline. Our result says the harness multiplier they report may be paid for by a token budget we do not have: Twin spends roughly 224,000 tokens per scored action.
WHAT_THIS_ESTABLISHES.paper_value: This is the open-weight data point the literature does not have, and it is a cleaner result than the certification-infeasibility scan because every mechanism is instrumented host-side and confirmed firing.

WHAT_TO_DO_WITH_IT: Do NOT ship max-harness. Do not re-run it whole.
Do NOT conclude the individual overlays are dead. Eleven variables moved at once and the counters localise the COST, not the blame.
The next test of any of these parts must hold ACTIONS PER GAME roughly constant, or it is testing the displacement and not the idea.
The interior-change arm is the right shape by contrast: it adds one honest observation field and NO model-facing machinery, so it cannot displace play.
AN_INSTRUMENT_NOTE_WORTH_KEEPING: Counters landed in artifacts/*_events.jsonl, not in viewer_data.json. The first place I looked, viewer_data.json, has an empty viewer_steps list and a lastEvent that is a plain action record. Download with the filter events.jsonl and read records whose type is experiment.
